label: punctuation: the full stop, comma, question mark and the rest
note: CLOSED BY CHAPTER 108, AND THE NOTE'S CLAIM WAS OPENED RATHER THAN TRUSTED. 'Modern Malayalam uses the European marks, and not one lesson teaches any of them' -- six lessons matched a punctuation grep and FIVE were 'command' matching 'comma'; the sixth, ML-C70-um-more, mentions ENGLISH's commas contrastively. True. NINE SPANISH POINTS (A1-O3-01..09) BEHIND THIS ONE, at zero new headwords and zero script debt. The marks were already on the page: ML-C02-ninre-peru-entaanu prints a question mark in its HEADWORD and ML-C72-ennu prints quotation marks around its quoted sentence, so each lesson opens where the reader has already seen its mark. The load-bearing fact is checkable: the Malayalam block U+0D00-U+0D7F contains ZERO characters of category P, so every mark here is borrowed, and the older answer is the danda that SA-C60-danda teaches in Sanskrit. THREE MARKS LAND ON JOBS MALAYALAM HAD ALREADY FILLED -- -um for the comma in a list, the question words and the -oo ending of ML-C03-sukhamaano for the question mark, ennu for the quotation marks -- and the recall drills exactly that. The Malayalam NAMES of the marks are deliberately not given: they exist and cannot be sourced here yet, the same call ML-S147-letter-ttha makes about stroke order.
